e: The Islamic Republic News Agency reports an "enemy" attack in Bandar Sirik.
A mass funeral is held for 110 unidentified Iranian soldiers killed in the Iran–Iraq War (1980–1988) after their remains were found on former battlefields.
Two Iranian nationals are convicted in the UK of spying on dissident journalists for Iranian intelligence with the intention of attacking them for their criticism of the Iranian regime.
Argentina's air force and navy are named "terrorist organizations" by Iran.
Iranian forces attack ship navigation systems on Didamar Island, Oman, causing an unknown amount of damage.

After judiciary head Gholam-Hossein Mohseni-Eje'i demanded action against what he called "abnormal behavior" on Iranian streets, Iran states it had detained a number of individuals in central Tehran for "promoting the abandoning of the hijab and public nudity."

France's ANSSI attributes a first-of-its-kind, large-scale sabotage cyberattack on 12 October—which spoiled food by spiking temperatures at 700 supermarkets—to IRGC-affiliated Shahid Kaveh group, adding that it found links to another IRGC cyber unit, Shahid Shoostari, to multiple French cyberattacks since 2020, including those targeting the Charlie Hebdo newspaper in 2023 and the 2024 Summer Olympics.
The United States evacuates its military aircraft from RAF Mildenhall following a reported threat from Iran.
Iran executes three individuals whom it accused of conducting operations for Israel and the US during anti-government demonstrations.
Iranian state media reports a strike on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz overnight, but claims no infrastructural damage.
Iran executes a Jaysh al-Adl member convicted of a fatal attack on a police station in Khash.

CENTCOM expands its interdiction efforts against the Iranian regime beyond its existing naval blockade by establishing Task Force Iron Gate to obstruct "illicit" shipments and weapons transit across land borders and the Caspian Sea.
Eight Canadian money services companies are sanctioned by the US for dealing with the Iranian regime.
The US cuts off money exchanger MEXC due to transactions involving the Iranian regime.
Trump announces that the US conducted "minor" strikes against Iran, targeting "a little bit of an anti-aircraft device."
The United States Central Command declares a $20 million incentive "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear program.
An activist is sentenced to death by the regime over his posts on X.
The US imposes new sanctions on companies and individuals in India and Turkey with ties to the Iranian regime.
Iran executes two people over their alleged role in killing two police officers in Isfahan during the anti-government protests.
A police officer is killed by unknown attackers in Saravan County.
Small-scale strikes are carried out by the US against Iranian positions on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran labels the United Kingdom's Royal Navy and Royal Air Force as terrorist groups, and MI6 as a hostile agency.
The IRGC states that it intercepted two commercial oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, claiming that the vessels struck naval mines after ignoring transit restrictions.

Iran rejects a new peace plan put forth by Qatari mediators on 28 October 2026, saying it was unacceptable and reiterating that its nuclear policy was unchangeable. In an attempt to resume peace talks, US Vice President J. D. Vance sends a letter to Iranian National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei that same day at Trump's directive.
The Iranian regime sentences Jafar Panahi for five years and one month imprisonment, seizes his assets, and prohibits him from leaving the country or using social media for two years.
The Government of National Stability in eastern Libya bans the entry of nationals from Iran and Afghanistan.

Sri Lanka rescues 40 Iranian sailors from merchant vessels in international waters near its coast after receiving a request from the Iranian embassy through diplomatic channels, citing medical emergencies.
A collision between a tractor and a sedan in Sistan and Baluchestan province kills nine people.

The US sanctions a Panama- and Greece-based law firm, stating that it facilitated Iran’s shadow fleet for years, indirectly supporting the Iranian regime's capacity to produce income to fund its nuclear program.
United States Department of the Treasury
Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei declares that the nation will completely bar the export of its enriched nuclear material.
The University of Tehran declares that female students who persist in breaching the hijab rule will be subject to disciplinary hearings.
The Islamic Consultative Assembly appoints Mehrdad Akhlaghi as Minister of Defence.
A German court imprisons two men convicted of plotting assaults against prominent pro-Israel public figures and spying on Jews for Iran's Quds Force.
The US issues new sanctions against Iran, targeting 16 individuals and 10 entities.
Iran hangs a man convicted for carrying out armed attacks in Kerman during the war, accusing him of supporting exiled former Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi and Israel.

At least two security officials, including a woman, are killed in separate instances along the border with Pakistan, with the government blaming the killings on "terrorist groups" sponsored from outside the country.
Iran executes a man found guilty of a 2024 Jaysh al-Adl attack on a Rask police station that killed 11 officers.
An IRGC projectile strikes the Panamanian-flagged crude oil tanker Gem No. 2 off the coast of the United Arab Emirates.
The US imposes additional sanctions on Iran's shadow fleet.
The US reports that it destroyed an Iranian-connected boat conducting surveillance after its crew was safely evacuated.
